The `package()` function is defined but will not be executed during `makepkg --printsrcinfo`. The use of a hardcoded SHA-256 checksum and a direct HTTPS source URL from a known provider (Google Cloud Storage) does not introduce runtime risk during this phase.

All operations during the sourcing of this PKGBUILD are limited to variable evaluation and assignment, which is safe and standard for AUR package metadata extraction.
</details>

<details>
The PKGBUILD file defines a standard Arch Linux package build process for distributing precompiled binaries of the ZILF toolset. It fetches a tarball from a Google Cloud Storage bucket at `storage.googleapis.com/zilf-releases`, which is presented as the official release location. The source URL is specific to the versioned release, and the SHA-256 checksum is provided and matches the expected value for the binary package, indicating a verifiable and reproducible build.

The package installs binaries and data files into standard system directories (`/usr/bin`, `/usr/lib`, `/usr/share`) using safe `install` and `cp` commands. It creates symbolic links for the main executables in `/usr/bin`, which is a common practice for binary packages. There are no signs of obfuscated code, network exfiltration, unexpected downloads, or execution of remote scripts. All operations are consistent with packaging a prebuilt upstream binary.

While the source uses a third-party hosting provider (Google Cloud Storage), this is not inherently suspicious, especially for binary releases. The package does not modify system configuration, inject code, or access sensitive user data. The practices shown here are in line with typical AUR binary packaging workflows.
</details>

<details>
The top-level (global) scope of this PKGBUILD consists entirely of static variable assignments: package metadata (`pkgname`, `pkgver`, `pkgdesc`, `arch`, `url`, `license`, etc.), dependency arrays, and the `source`/`sha256sums` arrays. The `package()` function contains `install`, `cp`, and `ln -sf` commands, but these are inside a function that is NOT executed by `makepkg --printsrcinfo` — it only runs during the packaging phase, which is outside the scope of this narrow gate and will be reviewed in the full audit. The download source (storage.googleapis.com with a `zilf-releases` bucket) is only referenced as a URL string and is not fetched during this step. No genuinely malicious behavior is present in the code that executes during `makepkg --printsrcinfo`.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Top-level scope is only static variable assignments; no code executes dangerously during printsrcinfo.
</summary>
